• THE. HORSFORIH MURDERER, Tinner,.the Horsforth murderer, was visited by his solicitor and made his will on Wednesday. He appears indifferent to his fate, and eats and sleeps well. Mrs: Turner, mother of the Horsforth murderer, has been removed from Armley to Wakefield prison to com- plete her term of twelve months' imprisonment, the transfer being effected in order that she may be spared ' the agony of hearing her son's death-knell rung. • BOWLS. Lowroic —A bowling handicap, in which there were 47 competitors, was brought to a close on the green attached to the flare and Hounds, Lowton, at the end of last week, when the prizes were awarded as follows: —l, Joseph Churton ; 2, James Woods; 3, J. Taylor. CROFT.—A. bowling main, between Mr. J. Worsley's team and Mr. W. Worsley's team, took place on Satur- day at Croft, with the following result :—Mr. J. Wors- ley's team 100, Mr. W. Worsley's team 139. The bowlers and their friends afterwards partook of an excellent knife and fork tea at five o'clock at the house of Mr. and Mrs. Maines. TERRIBLE BARGE ACCIDENT. FOURTEEN PERSONS KILLED AND TWENTY INJURED. NEW Yonn, WEDNESDAY.—A terrible accident occurred to-day on an excursion barge off Long Island. The • vessel,, which was heavily laden with 800 pleasure seekers, was struck by a squall, and the great strain suddenly thrown on the frame work of the barge caused the deck to give way, pinoning many of the unfortunate excursionists amongst the broken woodwork. Fourteen persons were killed and twenty injured. VTR WESTBOURNE PARK MYSTERY. TheWestbourne Park mystery aroused much comment lin London on Thursday. William Alexander Wynne, the husband of the woman found dead in the lodging in Golborne-road, was arrested and charged at Hammer- smith Police Court with murdering his wife by adminis- tering chloral. Evidence was given that the couple had led a most unhappy life, that they were both addicted to drink and frequently quarrelled, and that on aunday Wynne turned his wife into the street. On Tuesday night the landlady heard a thud, as though a body had fallen upon the floor, noticed the husband leave the house hurriedly, and later found the woman lying lifeless in the room with her dressing-gown torn to shreds. The prisoner was remanded. THE LIMEHOUSE TRAGEDY. . The coroner's inquiry into the death of Emily Maria Adams, who was fatally shot by her husband in the Railway Tavern, Limehouse, was resumed at the Lon- don Hospital. on Wednesday. The principal witness for the man John Alexander Lewis, who was in the company of the deceased at the time of the tragedy, and 'who was also stabbed by Adams. His evidedce was to the effect that he had been previously assaulted by Adams on account of his relations with Mrs. Adams, and that he had no doubt it was Adams who committed the murder.—After other evidence a verdict of "Wilful murder" against Adams, who is still at large, was ' returned. , THE ATTRACTIONS OF PWLLHELL Pwllheli, possesses all the requisite essentials for an admirable health resort. It is beautifully situated on the shores of Cardigan Bay, in South Carnarvonshire. The • strand extends for the length of about four miles. At low water mark the sea is not more distant than 60 yards. The beach, which is composed of slight shingle • and fine sand, gradually deepens. Bathing can be In- . dulged in at all hours of the day. Pure air, a good and sufficient supply of pure and wholesome water, uncon- taminated ground soil, good and wholesome food are all to be found here, and these four factors, which all sanitarians admit to be essential in a health resort, are all found at Pwllheli. • THE LIVERPOOL MURDERER.. Mr. Nicholson, district secretary of the Seamen and. Firemen's Union, on Tuesday, visited the convict John Conway in Kirkdale Gaol. It will be remembered that the condemned man some days ago addressed to the Home Secretary a petition praying for a reprieve on account of his services in the Crimean and other campaigns. On Mr. Nicholsou, informing him of the impossibility of inducing anyone to sign a petition on , account of the general belief in his guilt, Conway made strong protestations of innocence, and declared that the, murderer was a man who hired him to carry the sack to. the river, and paid him a sovereign.

THE FATAL GIN DRINKING. An inquest was held at Leeds, on Monday, on the bodies of two labourers named Bartley and Carmichael, who had died from the effects of excessive gin drinking. The gin, which had been stolen from Marsh-lane Station, was 22 degrees under proof. The jury returned a ver- dict of "Death from misadventure." The two boys who are alleged to have stolen the gin are in custody.

GENERAL BOOTH'S RECEPTION AT THE CAPE. CAPETOWN, AUGUST 11.—A meeting was held here yesterday evening in order to welcome General Booth, who had landed in the morning. The meeting was held in the largest building in Capetown, and the hall was closely packed with some five thousand people of all creeds and denominations. The appearance of the General was the signal for a perfect storm of cheering, and the reception was altogether a most remarkable one. DEATH OF THE OLDEST CHURCH DIGNITARY. The very Reverend Gilbert Elliot, Dean of Bristol, the oldest dignitary of Coe English Church, died on Tuesday, at Clifton, in his 92nd year. He had been Dean of Bristol for more than 40 years,having been appointed in 1850 on the recommendation of Lord John Russell, his relation by marriage. Dean Elliot, who was in his day a man of influence and efilinence among the Evangelical clergy, had before his promotion held the important incumbency of Trinity Church, Ma rylebone. He was Prolocutor of Convocation from 1857 to 1864, when he resigned that honorary post. But he never resigned his Deanery, although he had been for many years incapable of discharging its functions. Dr. Elliott was in his prime a man of imposing presence, and an eloquent preacher. He carried out the restoration of Bristol Cathedral at a cost of ninety thousand pounds. Mrs. Elliot is the well-known author of the "Diary of an Idle Woman in Italy," and many other works.
